openActions.title: Add mid-sprint dev–QA test-scope sync
openActions.description: FB-0005 shows QA scope misalignment late in the cycle; FB-0003 shows bugs reaching QA too late. A fixed mid-sprint checkpoint lets QA confirm coverage and dev flag at-risk stories before the final handoff.
openActions.teams: Dev Team, QA Team, Product Team

openActions.title: Require two reviewers on every release-path PR
openActions.description: FB-0006 calls for two reviewers on PRs. Making dual review mandatory on main and release branches spreads review load and catches issues before late-cycle QA churn.

openActions.title: Timebox daily standups to 15 minutes
openActions.description: FB-0004 reports dailies running too long. A 15-minute cap with a parking-lot channel for deep dives keeps ceremony discipline without losing blocker visibility.

openActions.title: Introduce a pre-QA merge checklist
openActions.description: FB-0003 highlights late bugs handed to QA. A short checklist before the QA queue reduces rework at the end of the sprint.

openActions.title: Align acceptance criteria with QA during sprint planning
openActions.description: FB-0005 flags test-scope gaps. Reviewing acceptance criteria with QA when stories are committed keeps expected coverage explicit from day one.

openActions.title: Document what worked in the recent release
openActions.description: FB-0001 and FB-0002 credit successful release delivery. Capturing the practices that worked gives the team a repeatable playbook for the next cycle.

reportExcerpt.themesSummary: Successful release delivery: The team reported strong collaboration during release week and delivered the milestone on the planned date. Late-cycle quality gaps: A recurring concern is that many bugs reached QA late in the sprint; feedback also points toward earlier QA alignment on test scope before formal testing. Process discipline (ceremonies and reviews): Daily syncs frequently ran over schedule, and the team raised ideas to tighten pull-request review before merge.

topicBreakdown.label: Successful release delivery
topicBreakdown.summary: The team reported strong collaboration during release week and delivered the milestone on the planned date.

topicBreakdown.label: Late-cycle quality gaps
topicBreakdown.summary: Feedback items highlighted bugs reaching QA late in the sprint and a need to align with QA on test scope before formal testing.

topicBreakdown.label: Process discipline (ceremonies and reviews)
topicBreakdown.summary: Daily syncs frequently ran over schedule, and the team raised expectations for pull-request review discipline before merge.

recurringTopics.label: Code review delays
recurringTopics.summary: Across four sprints, feedback items repeatedly cited idle review queues, slow turnaround on urgent fixes, and calls for stricter reviewer policies.

recurringTopics.label: Long meetings / planning
recurringTopics.summary: Feedback from Sprint 1 and Sprint 4 noted daily syncs and planning sessions routinely exceeding their allotted time.

recurringTopics.label: QA / testing gaps
recurringTopics.summary: Sprint 1 and Sprint 3 feedback items reported late-cycle bugs and a regression where integration tests missed a critical scenario.

recurringTopics.label: Sprint readiness
recurringTopics.summary: Sprint 2 and Sprint 3 feedback items pointed to stories entering the sprint without clear acceptance criteria and suggested readiness checklists.

recurringTopics.label: Deployment reliability
recurringTopics.summary: Positive feedback items in Sprint 2 and Sprint 4 credited stable deployment pipelines and reliable production releases.

limitations: Counts reflect feedback items, not individuals.
Recurring themes for RETRO-2026-002, RETRO-2026-003, and RETRO-2026-004 were inferred from seed feedback text only; no analysis was imported for those retrospectives.
Six anonymous feedback items may not represent the full team experience for Sprint 1.
Semantic matching across sprints identifies patterns, not proof of causality.
